item.title: Thursday, 29 October 2026: 10 stories
item.description:
Spain's minister slams an 'inexplicable' order — A Renfe train hit a stopped Iryo train near Urda, killing at least 68; the minister says control let it restart at full speed while a stop signal was active.

A war warning, then a letter to Tehran — The WSJ reports the US told Gulf allies to prepare for strikes on Iran after the midterms, and that JD Vance wrote to Tehran to revive talks.

Fed holds, but two want a hike — The US Fed kept rates at 3.75–4% in a 10-2 vote; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted another rise.

Netanyahu's bloc slips to 53 — With 85.6% counted, Netanyahu's bloc had 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48 and Arab-led parties 19; 61 are needed.

Cabinet clears a 3% DA hike — DA and DR rise from 60% to 63% from 1 July 2026, for about 48 lakh employees and 68 lakh pensioners.

Arnab's toll: five dead in Andhra — CM Naidu says five people died in Andhra; about 15,000 power poles and nearly 50,000 trees came down.

Jio ends day one 27% above issue — Jio Platforms closed its first day at ₹1,419, 26.81% above issue, even as the Sensex fell 353 points.

Investors balk at Google's AI bill — Alphabet's revenue rose 25% and Google Cloud doubled, but $51.4 billion of quarterly capex left free cash flow negative; shares fell about 10% after hours.

Britain's budget targets energy bills — Chancellor John Healey promised £100 to up to 20 million households in England and kept zero VAT on household electricity to July 2027.

Lula's rival flees to the US — Flávio Bolsonaro reached Miami after a Supreme Court judge ordered him to surrender his passports; he denies alleged money laundering.

item.title: Wednesday, 28 October 2026: 9 stories
item.description:
Cyclone Arnab makes landfall — Arnab crossed the Andhra and Yanam coasts between 2 AM and 8 AM, gusting to 150 km/h, then weakened; no deaths had been officially reported.

Netanyahu leads Israel's vote count — With about 42% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc had 57 seats, Eisenkot's opposition 47 and Arab-led parties 16; 61 are needed.

Iran says a tanker hit mines near Hormuz — Iran's navy says an unnamed tanker caught fire after hitting mines east of Hormuz; no one else has confirmed it.

Gas exporters close ranks in Moscow — Putin hosted the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, whose members say they hold about 70% of the world's gas reserves.

Syria shuts its Jordan border — Syria closed the Nassib crossing after Jordanian air strikes that it says killed seven people, including three children.

Jio debuts at a 21% premium — Jio Platforms opened at ₹1,358, 21.36% above its ₹1,119 issue price, after India's biggest IPO drew bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

OpenAI says its AI cracked big proofs — OpenAI says its models proved or disproved three major problems in maths, computer science and physics; outside experts are still checking.

News publishers vs the privacy law — 21 news publishers told the Supreme Court that India's data privacy law would force journalists to seek consent from the people they cover.

Netherlands quits Eurovision — Dutch broadcaster NPO will skip Eurovision 2027 in Bulgaria, citing division over Israel's participation.

item.title: Tuesday, 27 October 2026: 7 stories
item.description:
Arnab is now a severe cyclone — IMD put Arnab 490 km off Visakhapatnam, set to turn very severe and cross the Andhra and Yanam coasts by the forenoon of 28 Oct, gusting to 140 km/h.

Israel votes, Netanyahu trails — Israelis elect all 120 Knesset seats; polls gave the opposition about 52 seats and Netanyahu's alliance about 50, short of the 61 needed.

Gulf rivals meet in Tehran, no deal yet — Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish security chiefs met Iran's president in Tehran and agreed to keep talking; no deal was announced.

Houthis claim hits on Saudi oil pumps — The Houthis say they hit pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline and Riyadh's airport; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed either.

Sensex bounces, rupee slips — The Sensex rose 483 points to 73,606.75, ending a four-day slide, but the rupee fell 25 paise to 95.19 per dollar.

Anthropic files for a Nasdaq listing — Anthropic's public IPO filing shows $16.3 billion of revenue for January–June 2026 and an $80.7 billion net loss, $72.4 billion of it non-cash.

EC tells SC: SIR orders were unanimous — The Election Commission told the Supreme Court all three SIR orders were unanimous; petitioners allege the CEC overrode the other commissioners.
